name: Neros
summary: Neros develops autonomous drone and counter-drone systems designed for cost-effective, scalable defense deployment.
overview: Neros is a defense technology company building autonomous drone and interceptor systems, with a focus on scalable production and multi-drone operations.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Neros announced the capital to scale autonomous and interceptor-drone programs.

bull_case: Demand for low-cost autonomous and counter-drone systems could create a large defense market for companies that can manufacture reliably at scale.
bear_case: Defense procurement cycles are long and concentrated, while production scale, export rules, and hardware execution can introduce meaningful risk.
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: Neros builds autonomous drone and counter-drone systems for defense applications.
company: Neros develops autonomous drone platforms and interceptor systems aimed at countering larger drone threats. Its product strategy emphasizes cost efficiency and the hardware and software needed to coordinate multiple assets.
In August 2026, Neros announced a $250 million Series C at a $2.5 billion post-money valuation, co-led by Sequoia Capital and American Strategic Technology Fund.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Neros is a private-market signal for the shift toward autonomous, lower-cost systems in defense procurement. The investment case rests on manufacturing scale as much as software and autonomy.

changed.text: Profile reviewed against available public information.

takeaways: Neros is building autonomous drones and counter-drone systems for defense use.
Its August 2026 Series C raised $250 million at a $2.5 billion post-money valuation.
Manufacturing capacity and program adoption are the principal operating milestones.
Procurement, export, and hardware-execution risks remain material.
